title: regional-graceful-cutover-controller-with-traffic-ramping-and-variant-scrubbing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a controller that performs graceful multi-region cutovers by ramping live traffic into a standby region while running automated variant scrubbing on fallback model families. The controller must ensure latency and error SLOs during cutover, avoid model-quality regressions, and leave standby fleets warm enough to accept traffic within defined windows.

Background: We have several incidents where bulk region failover (e.g., capacity pressure or region outage) results in sudden latency spikes and unseen model variant regressions because fallback models were not vetted against our most common prompt families. Current warmup is binary (prefill on activation) and lacks traffic-aware ramping or automated variant curation.

Scope:
- A Cutover Controller component that orchestrates: traffic ramp schedules, traffic-weight decay from primary region, progressive activation of standby instances, and automated validation of fallback model variants (variant scrubbing).
- Variant scrubbing pipeline that runs a curated prompt set against candidate fallback variants, computes quality deltas, and quarantines variants that exceed configured regressions thresholds.
- Traffic ramp algorithm that considers real-time latency percentiles, KV cache warmth score, and available capacity to decide ramp increments.
- Safety gates: immediate rollback triggers for error-rate excursions, automated slowdown when 95th percentile latency crosses threshold, and hard capacity cutoffs.

Design notes:
- Controller state machine: PRECHECK -> ALLOCATE -> SCRUB -> RAMP -> STABLE -> FINISH. Each step has timeboxes and abort conditions.
- Scrubbing: use representative prompt corpus per customer tier and per route. For each candidate variant compute BLEU-like and hallucination heuristics plus token-efficiency delta. If delta > threshold, mark variant as quarantined and skip.
- Ramping: initial ramp epoch 5% traffic for 30s, double every epoch until target or a safety gate trips. Epoch length is configurable by policy and can be adaptive (longer if latency is volatile).
- KV prefill: issue prioritized lightweight prefix prefetches to top-N customers based on recent traffic; avoid saturating GPU bandwidth by limiting concurrent prefetch streams per host.
- Tier routing integration: high-tier traffic can be assigned stricter variant acceptance thresholds and faster ramp profiles.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: add cutover_id to all span traces and metrics. Emit ramp_step, scrub_pass/fail counts, cache_warmth metric, and variant_quarantine_reason.
- Dashboards: Cutover history, active ramps, per-region prefill saturation, and quarantined variants table.
- API: Expose manual start/abort endpoints and dry-run mode that simulates scrubbing and ramp decisions without changing routing.

Rollout plan: alpha in US-west with internal traffic only; follow with a staged rollout to two more regions after 2 weeks of stability and no regressions.

Risks: over-aggressive prefetch could degrade serving capacity; scrubbing false negatives could allow bad variants; slow scrubbing may delay cutovers. Mitigations are conservative defaults and operator overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can perform a full PRECHECK->FINISH cutover in a test cluster with configurable epoch timings
Variant scrubbing pipeline rejects variants that exceed configured quality regression thresholds in synthetic runs
Traffic ramp respects 95th latency safety gate and halts or rolls back when triggered
KV prefill activity does not increase 99th percentile GPU utilization beyond configured cap during ramp
Telemetry emitted for each cutover: cutover_id, ramp_step, scrub_results, cache_warmth, and final outcome
